record.context_brief: Dimension of extended replicativity solution space
record.original_question: Suppose λ assigns to each positive integer n a complex-valued arithmetic sequence λn(j), and consider the extended replicativity system (1/n) Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} φ((x+k)/n) = Σ_{j=1}^∞ λn(j) φ(jx). Is it true that the complex vector space of all solutions φ in L1(R/Z) is at most two-dimensional?

evidence.quote: Concerning extended replicativity given by 1/n Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} ϕ((x + k)/n) = Σ∞_{j=1} λn(j)ϕ(jx) consult [167] and [168] by L.G. Lucht.
Is it true that the C-linear space of all its solutions ϕ ∈ L1(R/Z) is at most two-dimensional?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ and let $L^1(\mathbb{T})$ denote the complex Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue-integrable, $1$-periodic functions $\varphi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$. For each positive integer $n$, let $\lambda_n:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$, $j\mapsto \lambda_n(j)$, be a fixed complex-valued arithmetic sequence such that, for every $\varphi\in L^1(\mathbb{T})$, the series $\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\lambda_n(j)\,\varphi(jx)$ converges (in the $L^1$ sense, say) and defines an element of $L^1(\mathbb{T})$.

Consider the "extended replicativity" system of functional equations
$$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\varphi\!\left(\frac{x+k}{n}\right) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\lambda_n(j)\,\varphi(jx),\qquad n=1,2,3,\dots,$$
to be satisfied for almost every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, simultaneously for all $n\geq 1$.

Let $V(\{\lambda_n\}) \subset L^1(\mathbb{T})$ denote the $\mathbb{C}$-vector space of all $\varphi\in L^1(\mathbb{T})$ which solve this system.

Question: Is it true that, for every choice of the family $\{\lambda_n\}_{n\geq 1}$ for which the above system is well-posed, one has
$$\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V(\{\lambda_n\}) \;\leq\; 2\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related work by Lucht on replicativity and function spaces and on arithmetic convolution equations, but no source was found that confirms or refutes the conjectured two-dimensionality of the $L^1(\mathbb{T})$ solution space for the extended replicativity system. The current status could not be verified from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Replicativity and Function Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Replicative functions as solutions of an infinite system, with degree of regularity (continuous, bounded variation, integrable) connected to the multiplicative arithmetical function u.
status_evidence.claim: Background reference on replicative functional equations in function spaces, but does not settle the dimensionality question.
